extraction_notes:
SCOPE / BUNDLE. clinical-studies. Five human studies (inclisiran S41; nusinersen paediatric S42 and adult S43; volanesorsen S44; QPI-1002/teprasiran post-bypass S60) plus one mouse study (S40) that the bundle brief assigned here. S40 is flagged study_type animal_invivo so it can be excluded from human-only analyses. n per arm is carried on every row because several of these studies are badly underpowered: n = 4 per arm (S44), n = 3 per dose cohort with n = 4 placebo (S60), n = 10 and n = 14 arms (S41), n = 12 and n = 13 coagulation subgroups (S43).

QUOTE VERIFICATION. All 74 measurement rows were checked programmatically: each verbatim_quote, and each severity_stated_by_source that is not NOT_REPORTED, was matched against the staged source file after stripping XML tags, unescaping entities, NFKC-normalising, unifying dash and quote variants, and collapsing whitespace. 74/74 quotes and all severity strings matched. Embedded quotations inside notes fields were checked the same way.

TABLE QUOTES ARE FLATTENED. S42, S43 and S44 are JATS XML on effectively one line; the tables were parsed by stripping tags, so a table quote reads as a bare run of numbers with the column structure gone (for example the S43 Table 3 quote 'aPTT (s) 2 12 18.2 28.8 - 2.1 0.04' is: SMA type 2, n = 12, 18.2 months observation, baseline 28.8 s, change -2.1 s, p = 0.04). Every such row names the exact table and the exact line in source_locus so a reviewer can realign the columns. Do not attempt to re-parse these quote strings positionally without the table.

CONTRADICTION 1 - S42, INR magnitude differs ten-fold between two loci in the same paper. Table 4 prints the linear-regression coefficient for INR as 0.009 per dose (t = 2.796, p = 0.006); the Results narrative and the Abstract both say 'INR increasing by 0.09 per injection'. Both are recorded as separate rows (readout_name INR_regression_coefficient_per_dose and INR_increase_per_injection_as_stated_in_text) with identical p-values, so a downstream user sees the conflict instead of a silently chosen number. Do not sum or average them. Internal consistency favours 0.009 (all INRs stayed within 0.8-1.2 over up to 10 doses), but the source never resolves it - this is a candidate erratum.

CONTRADICTION 2 - S42, Abstract versus Table 3 on APTT. The Abstract states 'There were no significant changes in platelet count, activated partial thrombin time, creatinine levels or liver enzyme levels during treatment', while Table 3 records a new high APTT in 10/46 (21.7%) patients. These are not the same quantity: the Abstract refers to the regression trend across doses (p = 0.565), the table to the count of individual excursions. Both are extracted, each labelled.

DENOMINATOR HAZARD - S42 Table 3. The footnote says the table shows shifts 'in those patients with normal baseline values', but the printed denominators (12 / 23 / 11 / 46) are the full group sizes. So 10/46 = 21.7% has a numerator restricted to normal-baseline patients over a whole-cohort denominator; the true incidence among at-risk children is higher. Flagged on every S42 shift row.

CONTRADICTION 3 - S44, platelet aggregation n. Results 3.4 presents agonist-by-agonist aggregation percentages 'for patients' versus healthy controls; the Discussion states 'Platelet aggregation was performed in only one patient, due to the impossibility of performing the proposed method with lactescent samples.' The aggregation row is kept but explicitly marked n = 1-versus-n = 4 unresolved. No p-values are printed for aggregation, consistent with the n = 1 account.

CONTRADICTION 4 - S44, regulatory status. The source asserts 'volanesorsen received approval from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for FCS treatment', which conflicts with the bundle premise that volanesorsen has no US label (EU/EMA approval as Waylivra). Recorded verbatim in the oligo max_phase field and flagged here rather than silently corrected; it matters because this paper is the main quantitative human haemostasis source for a compound whose severe thrombocytopenia has no US labelling.

MINOR SOURCE DEFECTS. S44 gives the patients' mean age as '56.5 +/- 0.5 years' in Results 3.1 but 56.5 +/- 13.2 in Table 1. S44 writes platelet counts as 'platelets/uL' for values that are plainly x10^3/uL (median 237.5 against a stated reference range of 150,000-450,000). S42 calls APTT 'activated partial thrombin time' in the running text and Abstract but 'activated partial thromboplastin time' in the table abbreviations. S60 contains the typo 'structually altered oligo deoxy ribonucleotides', quoted as printed.

ASSAY-COMPARABILITY WARNING - S41. Fibrinogen and FVIII in S41 are ELISA antigen concentrations (Cloud-Clone kits) reported in ug/mL and ng/mL, not Clauss fibrinogen (g/L) and not one-stage FVIII:C (% activity). The fibrinogen values (~50 ug/mL) are three orders of magnitude below normal clinical plasma fibrinogen. These rows must not be pooled with clotting-based fibrinogen or FVIII rows from other bundles. By contrast, FVIII in S40 was measured by 'an adapted activated partial thromboplastin time', i.e. a one-stage clotting assay reported as % of normal.

NO FIGURE READING. Nothing was read off a plotted panel anywhere in this bundle. Where a value exists only in a figure the row carries readout_value NOT_REPORTED with readout_is_qualitative true: S40 Figures 1A/1C/1D (individual mouse VWF, cholesterol and FVIII points), S40 Figure 2C (gene-expression heat map, the F8 row), S40 Supplementary Figure 1 (multimer densitometry), S41 Figure 3 (post-treatment marker values - the reason every S41 null row has a baseline but no post value), S44 Figures 1a/1b and Figure 2 (thrombograms), S60 Figures 1-3 (creatinine, complement, PK curves).

MISSING SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL. S40 states 'siRNA sequences, including chemical modifications can be found in Supplementary Table 1', but no supplementary file is present in the staged full text, so siVwf and siControl carry NOT_REPORTED for sequence, length and all chemistry. S43's Supplementary Tables S1a-m and S2a-m (per-injection values) are likewise unavailable, so only the Table 2/3/4 summaries were extracted. sequences_captured for this bundle is zero - no source in it prints an oligonucleotide sequence.

MODIFICATIONS ARRAY IS EMPTY BY DESIGN. No source in this bundle publishes per-position chemistry with a stated legend. S44 is the only one that names a sugar chemistry at all (2'-MOE for volanesorsen) and it gives no positions. Nusinersen's and inclisiran's well-known chemistries were deliberately NOT modelled, since they are not stated in these sources.

BASELINE ROWS versus TREATMENT-EFFECT ROWS. Several rows are pre-treatment baselines (S40 mouse strain VWF baselines; S42 Table 2 counts; S43 Table 2 values). These carry effect_direction NOT_REPORTED and say so in notes, because a baseline is not a measured null. effect_direction 'no_change' is used only where the source reports a measured null: 22 rows. In the two S40 baseline rows the study-level timepoint template ('96 hours after siRNA injection') does not apply - the quote makes clear those values are pre-injection - and this is stated in the row notes.

REPORTING SILENCE versus MEASURED NULL. Four rows record silence, not absence of effect: S40 bleeding (the authors raise overshoot bleeding risk in discussion but performed no bleeding assay), S42 bleeding (the strings 'bleed', 'bleeding', 'haemorrhage' and 'hemorrhage' do not occur anywhere in the staged XML - verified by full-text search), S43 bleeding (the word appears only as the rationale for counting elevations and in a description of other trials), S60 bleeding (no bleeding term in any AE table; the only possibly-related events were two Grade 3 perioperative anaemias, one of them on placebo). These carry readout_value NOT_REPORTED and effect_direction NOT_REPORTED.

REPORTING ASYMMETRY - S43. The shift-count table counts only elevations as pathological for aPTT and INR ('for aPTT and INR, only elevations were considered pathological (increased bleeding risk)'). Consequence: the statistically significant aPTT SHORTENING that the same paper reports in Table 3 is structurally invisible in Table 4. Anyone mining shift tables alone for this compound would see prolongation-only data and miss the direction that actually occurred.

STATISTICAL CAVEATS THE SOURCES STATE THEMSELVES. S43: 'No adjustment for multiple testing was done' and 'all statistical test results should be interpreted as explorative' - the aPTT -2.1 s subgroup result (p = 0.04, n = 12) should be read in that light. S43 also notes only 56% of patients had a baseline coagulation panel because these were collected mainly from hospitalised, more severely affected patients, which the authors name as a bias. S41 has no control group at all ('a single-center study without a control group due to ethical issues') and powered itself on a statin FVIII study (n = 8 per group for 80% power). S44 is cross-sectional patients-on-drug versus healthy controls, not before-versus-after, so drug effect and FCS disease effect are confounded.

CROSS-SOURCE OBSERVATION WORTH KEEPING. Same drug, same intrathecal route, opposite dissociations by age: in children (S42) the INR trend was significant while the APTT trend was not, with 21.7% APTT excursions and a clean 0/46 for high INR; in adults (S43) the INR was flat while mean aPTT SHORTENED significantly. Neither cohort had a comparator arm. Do not merge S42 and S43 into a single nusinersen estimate.
